standard_references.evidence: The supplied official-source excerpt identifies the SDMX Glossary 2.1 as a source for cross-domain concepts and states that cross-domain concepts should conform to specified names, IDs, representations and codelists. It explicitly gives OBS_STATUS as the concept ID for Observation Status and CL_OBS_STATUS as the associated codelist ID.

The supplied official-source excerpt shows the SDMX Global Registry codelist catalogue interface and confirms that codelists can be searched and inspected there; it does not confirm specific health-domain codelists for this report.

The supplied official-source excerpt shows UN M49 entries for countries and areas with numeric and alpha codes. The report areas are synthetic subnational-looking labels, so no direct UN M49 mapping is confirmed.

limitations: The report explicitly states that the mortality and hospital-bed data should not share the same DSD; the concept scheme therefore includes concepts for two distinct statistical structures without treating each table as a separate concept scheme.
Cause-of-death labels resemble broad ICD families, but no ICD version is confirmed in the report, so CAUSE_OF_DEATH is kept as a local/domain concept rather than a confirmed ICD concept.
The reported areas are synthetic labels; no authoritative geographic code system or version is confirmed for Northland, Centralia, or South Coast.
Hospital ownership categories are not linked to an external ownership-sector classification in the supplied evidence.
Exact SDMX cross-domain concept scheme identifiers and versions are not confirmed for all common concepts in the supplied official-source excerpts; gaps are preserved in local notes.
The report provides observation statuses Final, Provisional, and Estimated, but no authoritative status-code mapping is confirmed beyond the general SDMX OBS_STATUS concept evidence.
The report gives calendar years and a year-end stock definition for beds, but does not provide a separate frequency field.
